note: Build stages and twin designs for the Execution tab. Measured numbers are read by build_page.py from bench/results/twin_designs.json and bench/results/pairs_poc.json; this file holds the plan text only.

stages.makes: questions answered from exact 3D state, the agent loop (typed tool calls, last 4 views + move log, up to 10 moves), a grader for answers and every stated step, no AI judge; the agent loop's picture rule is replaced by the 2026-10-03 plan (watch-only: full history, at most 30; live slice: last 2 plus notes)
stages.now: 13 of 13 tests pass; perfect test agent 100%; lucky agent (right answers, steps 40% off) 0% on steps

stages.makes: 10 twin designs measured on a sparse and a cluttered test warehouse; proof-of-concept set D2 + D4 + D8, each with a D10 keep twin, built pair-first
stages.now: see the Twin designs sub-tab; 20 triples per test scene
stages.next: scale to all 10 designs (Twin designs sub-tab, column 'To scale')

stages.makes: five task families, each with its prompt word for word and one swept variable: binding (2 to 36 boxes), occlusion (camera from the side to behind the forklift), memory (2 to 10 picker steps, a picture every 2), soft loads (rigid steel to damp cardboard), frames (0 to 2 frame changes); answers from exact state, a flip and a keep twin each; the 3D page tabs under How it works
stages.now: binding: answer left at every box count, flip right, keep left; occlusion: bin hidden 0% from the side, 57% from behind, answer yes (flip no); memory: blue item in B1, B3, B4, B4, B4 after 2 to 10 steps, label hidden in every question picture; soft loads: steel 6 yes, 7 no, double-wall yes, damp no, wrapped no (page model); frames: picture left, premise left, answer right
stages.next: stage 1 renders the same layouts in Isaac Sim; soft loads dropped 2026-10-03 (Isaac Sim 6.0.1 deformables keep no lasting crush and have no static friction), the rigid part becomes 'add one item: does it tip within 3 s?'; the memory family moves to a picture after every step and the dependent-chain dial; the measured runs draw the curves

stages.makes: Isaac Sim 6.0.1 (pip, Python 3.12, own venv) loads SimReady Warehouse-01, exports every labelled object as a box into the scene file (repeated names not askable), builds the question triples, renders RGB + depth per view in priority order (start views, then views 2 moves away, then the rest), renders swap twins in their edited scene, and checks rendered depth against the scene file
stages.now: dry run on the Mac with a fake renderer: 20 triples, 984 views written, depth check 254 of 254; a 783-object test scene builds 20 triples in 9 s; 13 tests pass
stages.next: rent an RTX PRO 6000 (driver 595.58.03+, Ubuntu 22.04+, 50 GB) for a pilot capped at 1 GPU-hour that scores every stage; then watch-only episodes are rendered once for every model, and the live slice renders each view on demand while the model moves

stages.makes: a smoke test of the live environment first (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Kimi-K3, Qwen, Grok); then the headline sub-tasks 3.2, 3.5, 5.10 and 3.1 with the dependent-chain dial K = 1 to 30 at 6 levels and a same-length control chain: 6 levels x 40 items x 3 twins = 720 runs per sub-task per model, alone and mixed; watch-only runs get the full picture history (at most 30) at check-ins (steps 3, 9, 15 and the end), the live slice the last 2 pictures plus the model's notes; drift answers at steps 3, 9 and 15; medium thinking with a heavy-thinking slice; total API budget $2,000 for all providers, capped in code; a human-play page on the same pictures, scored by the same grader
stages.now: OpenAI and Fireworks keys work (checked 2026-10-03); Fireworks also lists Qwen 3.8 Max; Claude, Gemini and xAI keys still to add
stages.next: the smoke test reads real token counts and sets the spend per provider; then accuracy per dial level next to the guess line (under it = systematic error), the triple score, drift answers and parse failures; a no-image baseline and a label audit on a sample

stages.makes: about 50 triples where the agent moves freely (any step length, any turn) and Isaac Sim renders each view on demand; the same models and the same grader as on the frozen grid
stages.next: superseded 2026-10-02: every evaluation now renders live, so the frozen-grid check is no longer needed

stages.where: Mac and a small human panel
stages.makes: a scripted solver that gets exactly what each model gets, and a small human panel on the same pictures; both must stay at 95% or above at every dial level, or the level is fixed before it is reported
stages.next: build the solver with the dependent-chain generator; recruit the panel (see Rejection Risk B6)

stages.makes: after the headline curves: 447 episodes covering every pair of the 50 sub-tasks (443 triples + 4 pairs); the full model list; a human baseline; a label audit on a sample; release files
stages.next: done when: renders pass the depth check, the 447 episodes are built and scored, and the human baseline and label audit are done

stages.makes: a pool of about 50,000 episodes (every one of the 20,341 mixes about 2.5 times) with their renders, from seeds disjoint from the private test seed
stages.next: starts when: phase 1 is done; stage 1 has measured views per second and size per view; a scene-variety plan exists (object shuffles, more SimReady scenes); training seeds are fixed. Open: a small fine-tune to show the split helps, or release it as RL-ready data with its training value untested

twins.name: near pair, small move
twins.scale: needs scenes with many object pairs closer than 3 m (real shelving aisles); pick such pairs first

twins.name: camera move
twins.scale: already in the set; record each pair's move and turn; cap the move per scene size

twins.name: camera height
twins.render: a second and third grid height (3x renders)
twins.scale: render the grid at 0.8, 1.5 and 3.0 m; only above-or-below questions flip (visibility never did)

twins.name: object swap
twins.scale: already in the set; move two prims in the USD stage, render the start view again, re-export the scene file

twins.name: object nudge
twins.scale: collision-free placement within 2 m, then the same re-render as D4

twins.name: orbit 180
twins.scale: render the view facing the pair from the far side; moves are large (9 to 11 m)

twins.name: azimuth sweep
twins.scale: render views around the pair in 45-degree steps and keep the smallest that flips

twins.name: frame switch
twins.scale: already in the set; needs a third object visible in the same view

twins.name: occluder in or out
twins.scale: insert a crate prim between camera and object (or remove the blocker), re-render; rare in both test scenes

twins.name: keep-answer twin
twins.scale: already in the set: every pair carries one, making a triple
